newsitem.title: THAILAND: INSTANT VIEW - Thai baht flotation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Thai baht flotation.

text.p: Thailand said on Wednesday it would float the baht with immediate effect after months of speculation about changes to the currency system.
A selection of analyst reaction to the new baht system follows:
ANDREW MAULE, BANK SECTOR ANALYST, VICKERS BALLAS & CO PTE LTD THAILAND
"In the short term, it may weaken the baht and the market will take some time to settle down. But people will be more willing to convert (dollars) to baht after an initial pause.

I think the capital flow (picture) will start to improve. I think the Bank of Thailand will allow the market to determine the baht rate. It would be counter-productive for it to intervene again in short term.
CHIA WOON KHIEN, HEAD OF ASIAN RESEARCH FOR SKANDINAVISKA ENSKILDA BANKEN, SINGAPORE

"The Bank of Thailand seems to have been forced to float the baht or a de facto devaluation because of the financial and balance of payment crises. Perhaps this indicates that the two-tier market does not work as it stops foreign inflows when the country is in need of liquidity.

"The hardest hit would be corporates which need to repay foreign debt now. The immediate challenge is to restore confidence. In the longer term, the government must fully address the fundamental issues -- the structural change of the Thai economy, corruption and its competitiveness."
